summary: Olympic National Forest summit lookout, an L-4 or R-6 cab built about 1931-1934 and gone by 1967; sources disagree on build year and how it ended; no source describes remains.

facts.design: L-4 gable cab per three sources; 14x14 standard R-6 ground house per a structural inventory entry quoted by Forest Lookouts
facts.status_note: Cab removed, burned or destroyed in 1967, depending on the source; no source describes what remains on the summit

access.note: On Olympic National Forest land with its own wilderness area and a hiking trail to the summit; no closure described; no source describes the summit today

visit.trail_note: Seven-mile hike, reached by following South Shore Lake Quinault Road about 6 miles from Highway 101

events.note: Built on or before 1931 per WillhiteWeb; a newspaper item of August 30, 1931 already describes the summit residence. Build year conflicts with 1932 and 1933 (see resolved_conflicts).
Mr. and Mrs. F.B. Hall lived in the one-room residence as the summer lookout staff; the 1931 newspaper item calls it a Forest Service fire lookout station
Gile and Sadie Mead spent a honeymoon in the 14-by-14-foot glass house, per a 1933 newspaper item
Structural inventory entry: a wood 14x14 standard R-6 plan ground house was constructed on the Quinault Ranger District

Lookout house partially destroyed by the weather
FFLOS and Forest Lookouts say the house was removed
WillhiteWeb says it was burned as it was considered a safety hazard

corrections.proposed: L-4 gable cab (FFLOS, Fire Lookout, WillhiteWeb); a structural inventory entry quoted by Forest Lookouts gives a 14x14 standard R-6 ground house
corrections.why: The record names only R-6, but three sources call the cab an L-4 design and one gives R-6 only as a 1934 structural inventory entry

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLOS gives 1933 and Fire Lookout gives 1932. WillhiteWeb says built on or before 1931, and an August 30, 1931 newspaper item already describes the summit residence. Forest Lookouts also quotes a 1934 structural inventory entry for a 14x14 ground house. The story reports the disagreement and the 1931 occupancy.
FFLOS and Forest Lookouts say the house was removed in 1967. WillhiteWeb says it was burned as a safety hazard, and Fire Lookout says destroyed. The story reports all three.

notes_for_editor: Build year is disputed (1931 or earlier, 1932, 1933, and a 1934 ground house in a structural inventory). The record's design R-6 is only one of the readings. The record's height_m 4.3 is not supported by any source read, so it is left out of facts. The 1931 newspaper item gives the Halls' origins differently from WillhiteWeb (Iowa and North Dakota reversed); not used in the story. The 1943 Harold Deery entry is a photo caption, so treat it as weak. Access: no source describes the trail's current condition or the summit's remains; the WillhiteWeb trip report may be old. Map and photo links on firetower.org were not read (images).
